uncited: Iterate through each seen view image $I_i \in S$.
Render the absolute depth map $\bar{D}_i$ from the NeRF $F_\Theta$ for the camera pose of $I_i$.
Compute the relative pseudo-depth map $D^*_i = G_\phi(I_i)$ using the pre-trained MDE network.
Calculate the per-patch loss contribution using the aligned depths.
Sum the losses over all patches and all seen views.
*   **Computational Bottleneck:** Rendering full-resolution depth maps for every patch can be expensive.
*   **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of seen views, the number of patches, and the cost of MDE inference and NeRF depth rendering.
The patch-wise least squares solution is $O(N)$ per patch where $N$ is the number of pixels in the patch.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing depth maps for the current batch of views.
Patch-wise processing allows for lower peak memory usage compared to full-image alignment if processed sequentially.
*   **Limitations:** Relies on the quality of the pre-trained MDE network; patch boundaries may introduce discontinuities if not handled carefully.
*   **When to use:** When training NeRFs on sparse or unconstrained image collections where global depth alignment fails due to varying object scales or dominant foregrounds.
It addresses the issue that global scale fitting undermines local statistics, a problem highlighted in prior work [62] cited by the authors.
